items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewer lists 'Eldridge, Tommy Turk, Parker, Phillips, Hank Jones, Ray Brown and Buddy Rich' as part of a 'JPT thing' (JATP), and the interviewee confirms 'Yeah, that was a JPT thing.'

ctx.x: I have an impression, forgive me if I'm using this phrase, but would you call Lester Young a space cadet? Was see on another plane? Like, we are sitting in this room and he is sitting in this room but he is on another plane?

I think you would have to call them that. I mean, maybe not seriously but, the way he carried himself, the way he talked, certainly his style of playing put him on another level, certainly. So, that was the difference. It wasn't exactly here. He was, sort of, in between. Definitely. I left his playing. I can't wait to tell you about this one incident that happened. We were on a bus during J A T P. We had gone from one town to the other on a bus, instead of our regular mode of transportation. After the concert, I…
sounded like with his bad English, “Whoever taken my whiskey, I’m their mother’s very best man.” You know what that meant?
